verdict.rationale: Foreloop's documented workflow runs agent workers (Claude Code or Codex) in a checkout on your own machine. The globally installed CLI and `foreloop init` set the agent up to poll for approved tasks, and the Agents view tracks each worker. However, the Foreloop control plane is a hosted service reached via foreloop.com's MCP/API, and nothing documents self-hosting it. Missing for 10: container or VM deployment docs, a self-hostable Foreloop backend, and independent or hands-on corroboration of running workers outside a local machine.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can self-host agent infrastructure locally, in containers, or on my own VMs

citations.quote: You run an agent — Claude Code or Codex — in a checkout of your repository on your own machine.
foreloop init installs the task-executor skill into the checkout, which is what teaches an agent working there how to claim and report on Foreloop tasks.
The agent then checks Foreloop for approved tasks on a cadence and works them as they arrive.
Development, under Agents, lists one row per worker
